question: Up to how many days after a pregnancy ends is a death still officially counted as maternal mortality?
explanation: You've got this! A maternal death is counted if it happens during pregnancy or up to 42 days (6 weeks) after delivery from pregnancy-related causes. Keep up the great revision! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h1)

question: As a nursing student, how should you easily tell the difference between 'morbidity' and 'mortality'?

options.A: Morbidity is a statistic while mortality is a clinical diagnosis
options.B: Morbidity refers to illness while mortality refers to death
options.C: Morbidity affects only infants while mortality affects mothers
options.D: Morbidity is always preventable while mortality is inevitable

explanation: Think of it this way: morbidity means being sick or having health complications, while mortality simply means death. Simple and clear! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h1)

question: When public health experts calculate the Maternal Mortality Ratio, what is the standard denominator used?
explanation: Great to know for exams and clinical practice: maternal mortality ratio is always expressed per 100,000 live births. You're doing brilliantly! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h2)

question: Why do we often see higher maternal and child mortality rates in rural Nigerian communities compared to big cities?

options.A: Rural populations have a higher birth rate per family
options.B: Rural residents completely reject modern medicine due to cultural laws
options.C: Urban populations have stronger immune systems from birth
options.D: Rural areas have limited access to equipped health facilities and skilled birth attendants

explanation: Spot on! Bad roads, long distances, and lack of well-equipped clinics mean emergencies take too long to reach help. This is why community health nursing is so vital in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h2)

question: What is the number one direct cause of maternal death all over the world?
explanation: Severe bleeding after childbirth (PPH) is the leading global killer of new mothers. As a nurse, knowing how to spot and manage PPH can literally save a life! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h3)

question: A newborn baby fails to cry or breathe right after delivery. What do we call this emergency?
explanation: When a baby can't breathe on their own at birth, it's called birth asphyxia. Quick resuscitation is the key here—you'll practice this a lot in your midwifery postings! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h3)

question: What is the main reason midwives and nurses use a partograph during labor?

options.A: To record the baby's immunization schedule after birth
options.B: To calculate the exact date of conception for the mother
options.C: To monitor the progress of labor and detect complications early
options.D: To measure the exact blood volume lost during delivery

explanation: The partograph is your best friend in the labor ward! It gives a clear picture of how labor is advancing so you can catch trouble early before it harms mum or baby. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h4)

question: Why must nurses watch a mother and newborn extra closely immediately after delivery?

options.A: A high proportion of maternal and newborn deaths happen within the first 48 hours
options.B: The mother is usually discharged home immediately without any risk
options.C: Hormonal changes stop completely after the placenta is delivered
options.D: Newborns do not require feeding assistance until day three of life

explanation: The first 48 hours are the riskiest time for sudden bleeding, infections, or newborn collapse. Close monitoring keeps both mum and baby safe! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h4)

question: Which injection is routinely given to every newborn baby to prevent dangerous bleeding?
explanation: Newborns have little tummies that haven't built up clotting factors yet. Giving Vitamin K right after birth protects them against bleeding disorders. Excellent clinical knowledge to carry into the ward! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h5)

question: What is the wonderful benefit of placing a newborn baby skin-to-skin on the mother's chest right after birth?

options.A: It helps maintain the baby's body temperature and promotes early breastfeeding
options.B: It replaces the need for routine childhood immunizations
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of neonatal jaundice
options.D: It speeds up the delivery of the remaining placenta

explanation: Skin-to-skin contact is magical! It keeps the baby warm, stabilizes their heart rate, and helps them find the breast easily. Nature at its finest! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h5)

question: What is the recommended minimum time a mother should wait before getting pregnant again, to protect her health and her child's?
explanation: Giving at least 2 to 3 years between pregnancies lets the mother's body recover, rebuild her nutrient stores, and give the next baby a healthy start. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h6)

question: How does poor nutrition in a pregnant mother directly affect her unborn baby?

options.A: It prevents the development of neonatal jaundice entirely
options.B: It causes the baby to be born with complete immunity to infections
options.C: It accelerates the closure of the infant's fontanelles
options.D: It increases the risk of low birth weight and developmental stunting

explanation: A baby's growth depends totally on what the mother eats. Poor maternal nutrition often leads to low birth weight babies who have a harder time fighting off sickness. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h6)

question: Why are functional emergency referral systems so important for pregnant women in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policy requires all babies to be born in teaching hospitals
options.B: Patients prefer to pay higher fees at tertiary hospitals rather than local clinics
options.C: Primary health clinics cannot manage severe obstetric emergencies like ruptured uterus or eclampsia
options.D: Primary health centers do not keep any medical records of pregnant women

explanation: Local clinics are great for routine antenatal care, but if a life-threatening emergency like severe eclampsia happens, patients need quick transport to a bigger hospital with a doctor and blood bank. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h7)

question: Which of these options is NOT a helpful way to run a community-based healthcare strategy?

options.A: Educating local leaders on recognizing pregnancy danger signs
options.B: Mobilizing women for local immunization campaigns
options.C: Relying solely on tertiary hospitals without community outreach

explanation: Good healthcare goes to the people! Waiting in a big teaching hospital and ignoring local grassroots outreach leaves rural mothers helpless. You're smashing these questions! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h7)
